    : "Abstract: This section covers the Heading style in DOCX — its role as the primary structural mechanism that organizes a document's content into a named, hierarchical sequence of sections — and four scenarios: headings applied in correct sequential order, a heading level skipped in the hierarchy, a top-level heading absent from the document, and consecutive headings with no body content between them. The converter reads each heading level to construct the DITA map hierarchy, generating sub-maps, topic files, and topic type classifications from the heading sequence and the content that follows each heading."

    : "Abstract: This section covers Images and Graphics in DOCX — the primary means of communicating spatial relationships, component locations, interface states, and process flows that prose alone cannot convey — and twelve scenarios: image sizing thresholds, inline and block placement, images with captions, side-by-side images, images inside list items, linked versus embedded images, images inside text boxes, and alt text application. The converter maps each image to a DITA element with a required child; block images are wrapped in , and a Caption-styled paragraph maps to the element."

    : "Abstract:This section covers the Title style in DOCX — its purpose as the root publication identifier, and two scenarios: a correctly applied title and a missing title.
